title: A rare human life should not be spent asleep
subtitle: Raag Gauree · Ang 188
summary: The shabad begins by calling human birth rare fortune, then asks what life is worth without Naam. It presses past entertainment and display until the GurMantra is planted and the Name alone fills the heart.
whyItMatters: This is for the person drifting through a precious life as though there will always be more time. Hold this shabad when the day is dissolving into appetite or distraction, and it restores seriousness without panic.
takeaway: Treat this life as rare enough to center it on Naam.

lines.translation: This human body is so difficult to obtain; it is only obtained by great good fortune.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਮੁ ਨ ਜਪਹਿ ਤੇ ਆਤਮ ਘਾਤੀ ॥੧॥
lines.transliteration: naam na japeh te aatam ghaatee ||1||
lines.translation: Those who do not meditate on the Naam, the Name of the Lord, are murderers of the soul. ||1||

lines.gurmukhi: ਮਰਿ ਨ ਜਾਹੀ ਜਿਨਾ ਬਿਸਰਤ ਰਾਮ ॥
lines.transliteration: mar na jaahee jinaa bisarat raam ||
lines.translation: Those who forget the Lord might just as well die.

lines.gurmukhi: ਨਾਮ ਬਿਹੂਨ ਜੀਵਨ ਕਉਨ ਕਾਮ ॥੧॥ ਰਹਾਉ ॥
lines.transliteration: naam bihoon jeevan kaun kaam ||1|| rahaau ||
lines.translation: Without the Naam, of what use are their lives? ||1||Pause||
Eating, drinking, playing, laughing and showing off
- what use are the ostentatious displays of the dead? ||2||
Those who do not listen to the Praises of the Lord of supreme bliss,

lines.gurmukhi: ਪਸੁ ਪੰਖੀ ਤ੍ਰਿਗਦ ਜੋਨਿ ਤੇ ਮੰਦਾ ॥੩॥
lines.transliteration: pas pa(n)khee tiragadh jon te ma(n)dhaa ||3||
lines.translation: are worse off than beasts, birds or creeping creatures. ||3||
Says Nanak, the GurMantra has been implanted within me;
the Name alone is contained within my heart. ||4||42||111||

structure: It opens by calling human birth rare and refusing to treat it casually.
The middle strips away the glamour of eating, laughing, and display without remembrance.
It ends with the GurMantra implanted and the heart occupied by Naam alone.
